note: Opened (200, no paywall). Title exact; byline Venkatesh Nayak (Director, Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative); The Wire, Rights section; article:published_date 2026-10-09. All five quotes are verbatim. Corrected one point in 'shows': the Legislative Department sent the Home Ministry's application on to the Commission, which had not had it before, so 'sent it back' was wrong. Added what the article reports next: after 40 days the Commission transferred the competent-authority questions to the Home Ministry and the counts to the CEO, Bihar. The 50-day reply, the Commission's refusal to transfer, the four-week direction (para 186 of 2026 INSC 564) and the absence of any named authority or count are all in the text. The author's note names a Senior Advocate whose name was deleted; 'shows' does not name him. 'Law and the courts' fits, since the piece tests compliance with the Supreme Court's direction.

fix.shows: The author asked the Election Commission and the Home Ministry under the RTI Act on 10 August 2026 whether the Commission had referred electors it found not to be citizens to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, as the Supreme Court ordered in May 2026 to be done within four weeks. The Commission replied after 50 days that it held none of the information. The Home Ministry transferred its application the same day to the Legislative Department, which sent it on to the Commission, and the Commission then passed the questions to the Home Ministry and to the Chief Electoral Officer of Bihar. No reply named the competent authority or gave a number of cases referred.
